title.narrative: Sub-objective 2: Mitigating the impact of winter conditions in underserved areas through a multisectoral approach in Syria

description.narrative: ltpgtIn line with the 2022-2023 HRPs, this project contributes to Sub Objective 2 of this Allocation by providing winter-related humanitarian assistance in areas with demonstrated high needs and low response coverage. The Action aims to mitigate the impact of winter conditions in underserved areas by bridging a multisectoral approach to early recovery.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe response builds on TGH's five years of experience implementing ECHO, OCHA, and SDC-funded multisectoral projects in Syria. Targeted locations are prioritized sub-districts with high severity scores. In August-September 2023, TGH conducted field assessments and coordinated with municipalities, SARC, DoE/DoW, and other NGOs.Thus, TGH will intervene in 4 locations with an integrated WASH-Education-CP approach in Anjara and Hoteh (Daret Azza sub-district, Aleppo) and Moraba and Busra Esh-Sham (Busra Esh-Sham sub-district, Dar’a).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe final objective is to enhance community resilience of vulnerable communities to winter conditions in underserved areas through integrated education, protection, and WASH services.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtCommunities long-term WASH needs will be addressed through a) the rehabilitation of water and sanitation systems and b) rehabilitation of damaged schools, including WASH facilities and focusing on winterization needs. Access to WASH services will be sustained through solar panel installations and capacity building for water authorities when possible. School personnel and children will be encouraged to correctly use the rehabilitated WASH facilities, supported by hygiene promotion sessions and hygiene items distribution.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtRehabilitated schools will increase access to basic quality education, focusing on the needs of vulnerable OOSC and children at risk of dropping out. TGH will ensure the education quality by building capacities of teachers on education methods and SEL, and by providing NFE activities, including remedial, catch-up, and Self Learning Program classes.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtChildren and teachers' resilience will be strengthened by mitigating financial barriers to education and winter preparedness. This includes providing stationery for NFE sessions, teaching materials, and cash for transportation to teachers from remote areas. Crossline students will be supported to take national exams through the provision of hygiene and dignity kits. Community resilience and engagement will be strengthened through Community-Based volunteers and parents' inclusion and awareness.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn the Protection sector, TGH will provide psychosocial support, including risk education and recreational activities. Teachers will receive training on these topics, and awareness campaigns will be directed at parents. Special attention will be given to children with disabilities, early married girls, and child labor cases. Case management and referrals will be provided as part of Child Protection mainstreaming in areas lacking specialized services.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis Action will complement interventions by TGH and partners in surrounding locations based on coordination with local and international partners.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtProject revision: Additional assessments were carried out in Oct 2024 in the four schools. In addition to continuing NFE, case management, and PSS activities, TGH will install solar systems in three schools (Anjara School in Aleppo already has one) and conduct minor repairs, maintenance, and provide furniture and equipment in all 4 schools under this project. TGH will also distribute 1 additional school kit and recreational kit per school before exiting to ensure continuation of activities. These actions will also support Syrian returnees and Lebanese refugees in Aleppo (currently 9 children are enrolled in the 4 schools).lt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtltbrgtRevised value: 27,369 individuals will be reached, including 26,240 through WASH rehabilitations, 2,479 through Education (incl. 900 crossline students), and 1,453 through Protection (see anx 3b). The new numbers reflect ground realities, with increases for education and protection and a revision for WASH activity 1.1.4.lt/bgtlt/pgt
